findings.title: AC-17 command/args scan misses a split flag (--password VALUE) and env-style assignments inside a shell string (PGPASSWORD=...)
findings.evidence: Staging render + gateway args ["--password", "hunter2-real"] -> policy: OK. Gateway command ["sh","-c","PGPASSWORD=hunter2 psql -h db"] -> policy: OK. ARG_SECRET_RE needs '=' in the same item and is anchored at ^; DSN_PASSWORD_RE uses \bpassword= so PGPASSWORD= (no word boundary before 'password') does not match. The rev 3 contract line 32 says command/args are checked for credentials; these two common shapes pass.
findings.fix: In the command/args loop, also fail an item matching ^--?[a-z0-9_.-]*(password|passphrase|passwd|secret|token|api[_-]?key)[a-z0-9_.-]*$ when a next item exists (split flag), and drop the leading \b from DSN_PASSWORD_RE (or use (?i)(password|passwd|pwd)=[^\s&]) so FOOPASSWORD= inside shell strings matches. Add two bad fixtures via a TCR.

findings.title: AC-13 rejects USER 0 / 0:0 but accepts a root primary group (USER 1000:0)
findings.evidence: Only int(user.split(':')[0]) == 0 is tested. Rev 3 (X-7) treats root group as root at pod level (runAsGroup/fsGroup/supplementalGroups 0), so the image-level rule is inconsistent: a Dockerfile with USER 10001:0 passes.
findings.fix: Also fail when the gid part is present and equals 0 (or document gid 0 as allowed with a reason, e.g. OpenShift-style group-writable dirs).

findings.title: C4.4 context guard is name-based and not pinned on later kubectl calls
findings.evidence: The guard reads current-context once; every later kubectl call (get/create namespace, delete job, apply --dry-run) re-resolves the current context, so a context switch mid-run (another terminal) would act on the new one. A context named kind-* that points at a remote cluster is trusted by name. When cluster-info succeeds but current-context is empty (in-cluster config), the else branch prints 'khong co cluster', which is safe but misleading.
findings.fix: Pass --context "$K8S_CTX" to every kubectl call in the C4.4 block (a small kc() wrapper); optionally also require the cluster server URL to be loopback/host.docker.internal for kind-*. Adjust the skip message for the empty-context case.
